source.gn_args_common: is_debug=false symbol_level=0 is_component_build=false angle_enable_wgpu=false angle_enable_vulkan=false angle_enable_gl=false angle_enable_null=false angle_enable_metal=true

notes.why_a_source_pin_lands_before_the_artifa: This file is created in two steps on purpose, and the order is forced rather than chosen: a lock file's artifact hashes have to be the hashes of real bytes, and the bytes do not exist until a recipe pinned to a revision has produced them. So step one -- this -- pins the identity of what will be built (revision, gclient target_os, gn arguments, ninja targets) and is the single source scripts/build-angle-apple.sh reads them from. Step two adds `release` and `targets` with the sha256 of each published file, exactly as contracts/artifact-manifest/windows-angle.lock.json carries them, and scripts/fetch-apple-angle.sh checks those before any byte is trusted. Windows arm64 was built in the same order for the same reason.
notes.why_this_revision: It is what `fetch --no-history angle` resolved to on 2026-09-05 in .github/workflows/apple-angle-probe.yml (run 33948370655), which is the first and so far only checkout of ANGLE anyone on this project has performed. Three gn configurations were generated against it -- iOS device, iOS simulator and macOS, all arm64 -- and all three accepted the argument set recorded above (12554 / 12560 / 10125 targets in the resulting graphs), so the recipe is measured rather than guessed. Pinning tip-of-the-day is not a quality claim about that commit; it is the commit whose buildability was actually observed, and moving the pin means observing the new one the same way.
notes.why_these_gn_arguments: `angle_enable_metal=true` is the product: iOS has no GL framework to link, which .github/workflows/apple-sdk.yml measured by asking rustc for the link line of each Apple slice. `angle_enable_gl=false` is the one argument here that is a correction rather than a preference -- its default is TRUE on macOS (gni/angle.gni derives it from `!is_linux`) and false on iOS, so without it a macOS ANGLE would carry a desktop GL backend that EGL_DEFAULT_DISPLAY could resolve to instead of Metal, and the two Apple platforms would not be running the same renderer. Pinning the backend in the artifact is better than selecting it at runtime through eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT attributes: there is then only one answer, and it is in a file rather than in a code path. `angle_enable_vulkan=false` because no Apple platform ships a Vulkan loader and MoltenVK would be a second translation layer under the first. `angle_enable_null=false` because the null backend is a test backend nothing here selects; leaving it in is dead weight in a binary that ships on a phone. `angle_enable_wgpu=false` for the reason scripts/build-angle-windows.sh's header records: that backend alone drags in Dawn's vendored shader compiler, and migo does not use WebGPU. `is_component_build=false` so the output is the two shipping libraries rather than a constellation of per-component ones. `symbol_level=0` and `is_debug=false` because these are shipping bytes.
notes.why_shared_libraries_and_not_angle_stati: ANGLE publishes `//:angle_static` (libEGL_static + libGLESv2_static), and it is deliberately not what is built. Every presenter in this repository loads EGL at runtime and hands eglGetProcAddress to glow::Context::from_loader_function -- Android and OpenHarmony open libEGL.so, Linux libEGL.so.1, Windows ANGLE's own libEGL.dll. Linking ANGLE statically on Apple alone would make one platform resolve GL at link time while four resolve it at load time, for no gain the engine can use.
notes.why_five_configurations_for_three_platfo: `target_os="ios"` is not a complete configuration: gn's //build/config/apple/mobile_config.gni asserts that target_environment is one of simulator, device or catalyst, so iOS device and iOS simulator are separate builds. That is the same split an xcframework already forces, since it refuses a fat archive that mixes a device slice with a simulator one. On top of that, both the simulator group and macOS carry an Intel slice, because scripts/build-apple-sdk.sh builds the engine for those and the two xcframeworks are linked into the same application. The slice list is asked of that script rather than copied here.
notes.no_upstream_binaries_to_pin_instead: ANGLE (google/angle) publishes no official prebuilt binaries for any platform -- the same finding windows-angle.lock.json's why_self_hosted note records, checked again for Apple. So there is no upstream URL to pin, only a self-built and fully-provenanced artifact, which is what this recipe produces.
notes.what_the_products_are_and_why_they_are_a: ANGLE's own `angle_shared_library` template switches to `ios_framework_bundle` when `is_ios`, so an iOS build produces `libEGL.framework` -- a DIRECTORY -- and a macOS build produces a plain shared library. That is upstream's decision and it is the right one per platform: Apple accepts an embedded framework bundle in an app and rejects a bare dylib. A directory is not a GitHub release asset, so the published unit is one .tar.gz per platform rather than one asset per file, which is where this pin's shape differs from windows-angle.lock.json's. scripts/build-angle-apple.sh --archive packs them on the machine that built them, so what is published is the build's own output rather than a repackaging of an artifact download. The archives are not claimed to be byte-reproducible: gzip stores an mtime. The pin is trust-on-first-use, the model ohos-sdk.lock.json states plainly -- the hash proves the bytes have not changed since they were hashed, not that a second build would produce them.
notes.why_the_macos_libraries_are_not_repackag: The shapes above are not tidied up to match each other, and the reason is in ANGLE's source rather than in anyone's taste. libEGL does not link libGLESv2 -- `otool -L` on the built library names only system frameworks -- it opens it at run time under a name it composes against a directory. At this revision: src/libEGL/libEGL_autogen.cpp:41 asks for ANGLE_DISPATCH_LIBRARY with SearchType::ModuleDir; src/common/system_utils.cpp:221-234 appends "." + GetSharedLibraryExtension() and, on the iOS family only, "/" + the name again; that extension is "framework" (system_utils_ios.cpp:27) or "dylib" (system_utils_mac.cpp:26); and ModuleDir is the app bundle's Frameworks directory on the iOS family but libEGL's OWN directory, via dladdr, on macOS (system_utils_posix.cpp:198). So macOS needs libGLESv2.dylib sitting beside the libEGL binary, and iOS needs libGLESv2.framework beside libEGL.framework in the app's Frameworks folder. Wrapping the macOS libraries in framework bundles -- the obvious way to make one xcframework hold all three platforms, since `xcodebuild -create-xcframework` refuses to mix frameworks and libraries -- moves libEGL to libEGL.framework/Versions/A/libEGL, and the search follows it to a directory holding no libGLESv2.dylib. Nothing would fail at build time; the first symptom would be an application that cannot get an EGL display. The xcframeworks are therefore split along ANGLE's own axis instead, one per shipped library per platform family, and scripts/build-angle-apple.sh --print-loader-layout is the one place that answers what the layout has to be.
notes.patches_in_these_bytes: The published archives are the pinned revision plus every patch in engine/third_party/angle-patches/apple, applied by scripts/build-angle-apple.sh before gn runs: 0001 so ANGLE compiles for the macOS deployment floor, and 0002 so the Metal backend implements EGL_ANGLE_window_fixed_size, which upstream implements for D3D only. The engine creates its Apple window surfaces fixed-size and sizes the drawable to the onscreen canvas when that fits inside the window, letting Core Animation scale it; without 0002 the Metal backend re-derives the drawable from the layer's bounds times contentsScale before every drawable and overrides that. Adding a patch changes the bytes without changing the revision, so the release tag carries a patch-set suffix (angle-apple-52f59428-p2) rather than reusing the revision's own tag, whose archives stay what they were.
